subject: Payrollio inference costing recap & decision path
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Payrollio inference costing recap & decision path

Hi Leah — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap while items are fresh and a proposed next-step plan. 

Pain points you shared
- High per-record inference spend for bulk payroll runs (peak runs: ~500k records/month).
- Latency spikes during month-end batch processing causing customer SLA hits.
- Lack of predictable spend model for the ML features (we heard $10k–$15k/month cap).

Goals you outlined
- Reduce inference spend to fit within the stated $12k monthly budget (hard constraint for Q3).
- Keep month-end latency below 3s/record for the core payroll-validate flow.
- Pilot within 6 weeks and prove token reductions and SLA improvement.

Redwood levers we discussed (high level)
- Batching: aggregate per-run requests to amortize KV cache and reduce per-token overhead. Estimated 30–50% tokens saved depending on grouping.
- Prefix / KV caching: persist common templates and contextual tokens across payroll runs to avoid re-sending large prompt prefixes.
- Model routing: route low-risk validations to a smaller, quantized model and reserve top-tier model for edge cases.
- Dedicated capacity for month-end peaks (predictable pricing) vs. hosted bursts.
- Quantization profiles: FP16/int8 where acceptable to cut GPU cost per token.

Initial TCO anchors (very rough, ballpark)
- Current: ~1.1B tokens/month (~$18k estimate at current throughput mix).
- With batching + KV caching: 40% token reduction -> ~660M tokens -> ~$10k estimate.
- With additional model routing & quantization: down to $6k–$8k (depends on accuracy guardrails).

Attachments: I included a short spreadsheet with the anchor math (20260721-payrollio-econ-anchors.xlsx).

Immediate asks for you / procurement
1) Confirm the firm monthly budget ceiling (you mentioned $12k) and whether that is net of platform fees.
2) Share a short sample of average prompt sizes (anonymized) and the monthly count distribution (daily and month-end peak).
3) Confirm decision timeline and whether procurement needs any additional compliance docs (I attached a common procurement questionnaire we usually return).

Proposed next step
- 30 min follow-up on Thu to align on pilot success criteria + go/no-go gates. If that works I’ll prepare a scoped 6-week pilot plan with a fixed budget cap and rollback policy.

Thanks — I’ll wait to confirm the follow-up time.

Best,
Avery Johnson

Avery — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. Quick answers: 

- Budget: $12k/month is our hard cap for inference for this project for Q3 (that number must include any platform fees).
- Sample data: I can share anonymized prompt/usage samples by EOD tomorrow (will remove PII).
- Decision timeline: Procurement needs an approved SOW and purchase order by 31-Jul to start in Aug.
- Compliance: procurement@payrollio.com attached a short list of required evidence (SOC 2 scope, data retention, encryption in transit). See attached.

We are open to a 6-week pilot if it reliably demonstrates the token reductions and keeps month-end latency within your proposed SLA. Key success metrics for our side: monthly spend <= $12k and month-end 95th percentile latency <3s.

Leah — appreciate the quick confirmation and the procurement list. A couple of concrete commitments from our side and the pilot framing.

What Redwood will deliver for a 6-week pilot (scope draft)
- Scoped traffic: up to your current month-end volume (we’ll confirm exact numbers after you share usage samples).
- Fixed pilot budget cap: $9,000 (we’ll include a clause that caps spend; any overage pauses the pilot).
- Expected impact targets: 35–55% token reduction from batching + KV caching in weeks 1–3, then iterative model routing/quantization to push toward 50%+ by week 6.
- SLA objective: 95th percentile latency < 3s for the validated flow. If we miss by more than 25% for two consecutive weeklies, we’ll trigger a remediation plan and credit.
- Deliverables: weekly token & latency dashboards, a final ROI readout, and a package of configuration changes for production rollout.

We’ll provide the SOC 2 summary, subprocessor list, and encryption-in-transit doc by EOD; procurement PDF looks good — we’ll fill and return.

Next steps
1) I’ll schedule the Thu 30-min alignment (propose Thu 10:00–10:30 PT).
2) Marissa, can you prepare a short priced SOW that reflects the $9k pilot cap and the rollback terms?
3) Rishi, please prepare a quick ops note on dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for month-end peaks (2-paragraph summary we can send to procurement).

Leah — if Thu 10:00 PT works, I’ll send the calendar invite plus the HubSpot SOW draft link.

Best,
